business_model.basis: stated in the 10-K Item 1 business overview
business_model.claim: The company sells natural gas, NGLs and oil produced from mature, long-life US assets. It also transports and markets these products.
quotes: We are engaged in the production, transportation, and marketing of natural gas, NGLs, and oil, managing a diversified portfolio of mature, long-life assets.

business_model.basis: stated in the income statement revenue lines; the ranking is read from those lines

business_model.basis: stated in the 10-K Item 1 text; no segment note is in the packet
business_model.claim: The filings describe operations by geographic operating area (Appalachian, Central, Other), not by reporting segment. Appalachia spans Ohio, Pennsylvania, Virginia, West Virginia, Kentucky, Tennessee and Alabama. The Central Region covers Texas, Oklahoma, New Mexico, Louisiana and Arkansas.
quotes: Our assets are located in the United States within the following geographical operating areas:

business_model.basis: stated in the 10-Q MD&A; the mechanism is inferred from its price and volume table
business_model.claim: Third-quarter commodity revenue rose year on year because of both higher realized prices and higher volumes. Management attributes the volume rise mainly to acquisitions and non-operated development.
quotes: The increase was primarily related to the 19% increase in average realized sales prices, excluding the impact of derivatives settled in cash, and the 5% increase in sold volumes primarily due to the acquisitions and non-operated development as discussed above.

business_model.basis: stated in the 10-Q MD&A and income statement; the mechanism is inferred from the derivative tables
business_model.claim: Hedging is central to realized pricing. About 80% of production is fixed through derivatives over the next twelve months. In Q3 settlements cut the total realized price per Mcfe from $4.29 to $4.02, and mark-to-market losses pushed GAAP total revenue down to 108,512 (table in thousands).
quotes: As of September 30, 2026, approximately 80% of our production was fixed through commodity derivative contracts over the next twelve months.

business_model.basis: stated in the 10-K, the 10-Q MD&A and the 8-K
business_model.claim: Growth comes mainly from buying producing wells rather than drilling. The company contributes limited development capital. A pending Birch Permian acquisition of about $1.8 billion is expected to close in Q4 2026.
quotes: We aim to obtain proved developed producing wells through acquisitions in accordance with our growth strategy rather than through development activities.

business_model.claim: Lease operating expense is the largest cash cost line. It was 135,916 (table in thousands) in Q3, or $1.24 per Mcfe against $1.21. Management ties the rise to the Canvas and Sheridan acquisitions and to greater liquids exposure.
quotes: The increase in LOE and LOE per Mcfe was primarily driven by the acquisition of Canvas in the fourth quarter of 2025 and the acquisition of Sheridan in the second quarter of 2026.

business_model.basis: stated in the statements; the link to acquisitions is inferred from the 10-Q MD&A
business_model.claim: Other costs that track the asset base and acquisition-funded debt are depletion, interest and asset retirement. Nine-month DD&A was 317,127 and interest expense 185,851 (table in thousands). Accretion of asset retirement obligations was 40,100, against asset retirement obligations of 869,966 on the balance sheet. The company runs its own plugging subsidiary.
quotes: In addition to our work on our producing wells, we have an extensive and innovative asset retirement program that consists of a vertically integrated plugging company based in our Appalachian Region.

business_model.basis: stated in the release and statements; the mechanism is inferred
business_model.claim: Financing relies heavily on asset-backed and amortizing debt, with a 2.66x leverage ratio against a 2.0x to 2.5x target. Long-term debt, net was 2,997,872 (table in thousands). Nine-month operating cash flow of 393,305 (table in thousands) covered capital expenditures of 137,674, dividends of 63,560 and buybacks of 94,680.
quotes: Consolidated debt consisted of ~72% in deleveraging non-recourse ABS and amortizing notes at quarter end.
